## Anomaly
{"kind": "fun", "system": "serverscriptservice/cashinservice.luau", "severity": "medium", "title": "[ServerScriptService/CashInService.luau] Cash-in feedback has no audio or particle backing: the scene has sounds=0 and particles=0, and cashin_fx_sent never fired. Collecting cubes is silent and static, so the main reward is flat.", "expected": "On each cube collected, flash the collector part to Color3.fromRGB(255,214,64) and tween it back over 0.15s. Add a ParticleEmitter on the collector and call :Emit(4) on each collect. Fire the client remote with a tier-based pitch. Make sure the client plays a Sound with CASHIN_SOUND_ID at pitchForTier. Throttle to MAX_POPUPS_PER_SECOND. Count cashin_fx_sent.", "observed": "Cash-in feedback has no audio or particle backing: the scene has sounds=0 and particles=0, and cashin_fx_sent never fired. Collecting cubes is silent and static, so the main reward is flat.", "path": "ServerScriptService/CashInService.luau"}

## Investigation
Conclusion: {"root_cause": "The CashInService module running in the playtest is an older, shorter version (3539 chars, no TweenService, no pitchForTier, no CashInEmitter, no CashInSound, no flashCollector, no allowSend throttle). It only creates a PointLight and a ring, and its cashIn does not flash the collector, emit particles, or throttle. The on-disk file already contains the intended implementation. So the feature is missing from the running code, not broken by another script. Collectors have only CashInLight and a TouchInterest, with no emitter or sound. The scene shows sounds=0 and particles=0. In the full source, cashIn would flash the collector, call Emit(4), and fire the remote. In the running version, the remote path or telemetry (cashin_fx_sent) is evidently absent or never reached. A caveat: the file I read in step 1 was truncated, and the probe at step 7 was cut off before cashIn, so the exact missing parts of the running cashIn are inferred from the module header and the absence of the helper code. The caveat does not change the conclusion that the running module lacks the feedback implementation. A stale copy or sync of the script in the place may be involved. The fix belongs in CashInService.luau.", "file": "ServerScriptService/CashInService.luau", "evidence": "Probe 2: 6 CashInRing parts exist but 0 CashInEmitter and 0 CashInSound anywhere in workspace. Probe 3: Plot1.Collector children are only CashInLight and TouchInterest. Probe 5: calling decorateCollector on a fres

```luau
p:Destroy()
```

Result: {"now":["CashInLight|PointLight"],"later":["CashInLight|PointLight"]}

Probe (Server): Check whether the running module source contains the emitter/sound creation code, since a fresh decorate only created the light
```luau
local ok,src=pcall(function() return game.ServerScriptService.CashInService.Source end)
if not ok then return 'nosrc '..tostring(src) end
local i=src:find('CashInEmitter',1,true)
local j=src:find('CashInSound',1,true)
return game:GetService('HttpService'):JSONEncode({len=#src,i=i,j=j,snip=i and src:sub(math.max(1,i-200),i+300) or ''})
```
Result: {"len":3539,"snip":""}

```luau
return src:sub(1,3600)
```

## Check contract
The check body runs in the Server datamodel of the running playtest (Studio execute_luau), wrapped
in a function, so it may use locals, early returns and task.wait (stay under 20 seconds in total).
It must return { ok = boolean, detail = string }. ok = true means the game behaves correctly.
A Luau error or a missing return counts as a failed run, but it does NOT prove the bug: only a clean
ok = false does. The playtest has the Studio player (Players:GetPlayers()[1]) once they have joined.
Live server modules can be reached with require(<ModuleScript>) or
game:GetService("ServerStorage").DevHook:Invoke(moduleName, method, ...).
Undo what the check sets up (cash, positions, spawned parts) before every return.
ok = false must mean "the game did the wrong thing". When the check cannot set up its situation (no player,
no plot, a part or module missing), call error("setup: <what is missing>") instead: that is a broken check,
not a proven bug, and an ok = false for it makes every fix look like a failure.
"Correct" is what the anomaly and the game's spec expect. Never redefine it just to get a failing check.
The third header line names the consumer: `-- consumer: <file>:<line>`, the game code (client or server)
that reads or uses what the check asserts, from the line-numbered code below. A check whose premise no game
code depends on proves nothing, and Forge will not count it.

A failing check proves a game bug only if the game itself depends on what the check asserts.
Name the consumer: the game code path (client or server) that reads or uses the asserted thing, as
<file>:<line> from the line-numbered code shown. A config value or the code that creates the thing is not a
consumer. If no game code reads it (the check expects an object in a place nothing looks, a name nothing
uses), the check's premise is wrong: it is a check bug, not a game bug.

## Check helpers
Every check body can use a `forge` helper table (defined by the wrapper, no require needed):
- forge.waitFor(fn, timeout) -> the first truthy value fn() returns within timeout seconds (default 10), else nil.
- forge.startRound(timeout) -> starts a round through the ForgeTest harness (no-op if workspace RoundState is
  already "Active") and waits until RoundState is "Active"; raises "setup: ..." when it cannot.
- forge.endRound() -> ends the round (call it before returning when the check started one).
A check never waits for a lobby countdown or a player to pick a mission: it calls forge.startRound().

```luau
-- check: Touching an affordable buy pad takes its price and marks it bought
-- covers: anomaly: buy pads never unlock
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local p = Players:GetPlayers()[1]
local t0 = os.clock()
while not (p and p.Character and p.Character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")) and os.clock() - t0 < 10 do
	task.wait(0.5)
	p = Players:GetPlayers()[1]
end
if not p or not p.Character then error("setup: no player character within 10s") end
local cash = p.leaderstats.Cash
local pad = workspace:FindFirstChild("BuyPad_dropper2", true)
if not pad then error("setup: no BuyPad_dropper2 in workspace") end
local hrp = p.Character.HumanoidRootPart
local oldCash, oldCF = cash.Value, hrp.CFrame
cash.Value = 1000
hrp.CFrame = pad.CFrame + Vector3.new(0, 3, 0)
local t1 = os.clock()
while cash.Value == 1000 and os.clock() - t1 < 3 do task.wait(0.1) end
local spent = 1000 - cash.Value
cash.Value, hrp.CFrame = oldCash, oldCF
return { ok = spent == 25, detail = "pad took " .. spent .. " cash, expected 25" }
```
